defaults:
set -u

# The model used to be a config key. A recipe that still sets it would
# otherwise be ignored silently, so refuse it.

# The generation floor used to be set here too, as a server-side env var that
# the baked run_vllm_serve.py never read. It now travels with every request:
# set logit-distill's gold_config.min_completion_length, which the trainer sends
# as min_tokens. Refused rather than ignored, so a recipe that still sets it
# does not believe it has a floor it may not have.


# The image's venv is not on PATH by default; the dispatcher runs this
# with `bash <file>` (non-login), so this export sticks.
PYBIN="python"

# Source: baked into the shared GPU image, no clone. Both paths are
# fixed by steps/train/distill/images/gpu/Dockerfile's own COPY/ENV lines.
CODE_DIR="${DISTILL_HOME:?DISTILL_HOME is set by the image}"
# PYTHONPATH=/opt/distill/src is already set by the image
# itself; nothing to export here.

# GPU allocation check (ibm-granite/granite.build#604). On Slurm 25.11.x an
# --overlap job step -- SkyPilot's container keeper is one -- can be granted
# fewer of the job's GPUs than the job holds (SchedMD bug 24862, fixed in
# 26.05.3), and the container keeps the keeper's device set. Ranks past the
# visible count would then bind a GPU another rank already holds and fail
# later, far from the cause. Refuse here instead. `nvidia-smi -L` lists what
# the container's device cgroup grants and ignores CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; a
# failed or missing nvidia-smi (0 listed) proves nothing, so only an
# undercount it reports is refused. Nothing is rewritten or worked around:
# the check holds whether the fix lands in Slurm or in SkyPilot.
GPU_WANT="${SKYPILOT_NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE:-0}"
case $GPU_WANT in ''|*[!0-9]*) GPU_WANT=0 ;; esac
GPU_SEEN="$(nvidia-smi -L 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^GPU ' || true)"
case $GPU_SEEN in ''|*[!0-9]*) GPU_SEEN=0 ;; esac
GPU_DEVS="$(ls /dev/nvidia[0-9]* 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
echo "student-rollout-generator: gpu check: allocated=$GPU_WANT visible=$GPU_SEEN CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-<unset>}' SLURM_JOB_GPUS='${SLURM_JOB_GPUS:-}' SLURM_STEP_GPUS='${SLURM_STEP_GPUS:-}' devices='$GPU_DEVS'"
if [ "$GPU_SEEN" -ge 1 ] && [ "$GPU_SEEN" -lt "$GPU_WANT" ]; then
  echo "student-rollout-generator: FATAL: $GPU_WANT GPU(s) were allocated (SKYPILOT_NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE) but this container can access only $GPU_SEEN (nvidia-smi -L). On SLURM this is ibm-granite/granite.build#604; rerun, or report the node." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# SKYPILOT_NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE is what SkyPilot sets on every backend.
# NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE is not set by anything; reading only it made a
# 1-GPU server start 8 data-parallel ranks and crash in vLLM's
# CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES split.
GPUS="${SKYPILOT_NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE:-${NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE:-8}}"
PORT="8001"
DP=""
[ -n "$DP" ] || DP="$GPUS"

# vLLM binds an AF_UNIX socket at $VLLM_RPC_BASE_PATH/<uuid4>, and
# defaults it to TMPDIR. AF_UNIX paths are capped at 108 bytes and
# ZeroMQ refuses anything over 107 — the reference launcher measured a
# default TMPDIR yielding 111, failing AFTER the engine had started
# loading. Keep this short and per-job.
export VLLM_RPC_BASE_PATH="/tmp/vllm-${USER:-gb}-${SKYPILOT_INTERNAL_JOB_ID:-nojob}"
export TMPDIR="$VLLM_RPC_BASE_PATH"
mkdir -p "$VLLM_RPC_BASE_PATH"

# Surface the SkyPilot cluster name for the teardown target, in the
# shipped monitor's generic ARTIFACT_STATE form so this step needs no
# scrape rule of its own. GB_SKYPILOT_CLUSTER_NAME is injected by
# launch_skypilot. Its OWN log line, separate from the URL marker
# below: get_events_from_log_line reassigns log_line after a matching
# config, so two markers must never share a line.
echo "GB_ARTIFACT_ID:cluster_name GB_ARTIFACT_STATE:${GB_SKYPILOT_CLUSTER_NAME:-unknown}"

# The address to advertise. A hostname is not enough: the consumer is
# in a DIFFERENT allocation, so this must resolve from there. Prefer
# the IP, resolved the way distill-gold resolves MASTER_ADDR (/etc/hosts,
# then getent), because that is the validated path on this cluster.
HOST="$(hostname)"
ADDR="$(grep -w "$HOST" /etc/hosts 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1; exit}')"
if [ -z "$ADDR" ]; then
  ADDR="$(getent ahostsv4 "$HOST" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1; exit}')"
fi
[ -n "$ADDR" ] || ADDR="$HOST"
echo "student-rollout-generator: serving on $ADDR:$PORT ($DP-way data parallel over $GPUS GPU(s))"

# Background, NOT exec: the URL must be published only once the server
# answers /health, and an exec'd process cannot echo afterwards.
# Publishing on start instead would defeat the whole design — the
# trainer would dispatch and race a multi-minute model load.
"$PYBIN" -m gb_steps_post_training.distillation.run_vllm_serve \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --model "/models/student" \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size "$DP" \
  --log_level warning \
  --max-model-len 16384 &
SERVER_PID=$!

# Wait for readiness, with a death check. Unlike the reference
# launcher, whose pid was a local blaunch rather than the remote
# python, SERVER_PID here is a direct child — so `kill -0` is
# authoritative and no log-scraping heuristic is needed.
DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + 1800 ))
while :; do
  if ! kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    # `|| RC=$?`, not `; RC=$?`: the launcher runs this block under
    # `set -eu`, so a bare failing wait would exit before the report.
    RC=0; wait "$SERVER_PID" || RC=$?
    echo "student-rollout-generator: FATAL: server exited with $RC before becoming healthy" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if "$PYBIN" -c "
import sys, urllib.request
try:
    urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health/', timeout=5)
except Exception:
    sys.exit(1)
" 2>/dev/null; then
    break
  fi
  if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$DEADLINE" ]; then
    echo "student-rollout-generator: FATAL: not healthy after 1800s" >&2
    kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 10
done

# Healthy. Publishing the URL now is what makes the dependency graph
# the health gate: the consumer target cannot dispatch until this
# binding resolves. Matched by the shipped skypilot monitor's generic
# ARTIFACT_STATE rule, so this step needs no scrape config of its own.
echo "student-rollout-generator: healthy after $(( $(date +%s) - (DEADLINE - 1800) ))s"
echo "GB_ARTIFACT_ID:vllm_url GB_ARTIFACT_STATE:http://${ADDR}:${PORT}"

# Hold the allocation for the server's lifetime. It never returns on
# its own; the teardown target is what normally ends it.
#
# Every way out of this section exits non-zero, so a server that dies
# before the teardown target ends it -- idle kill, OOM, crash, the cap
# below -- leaves its target FAILED. That matters on a build retry:
# gbserver reuses SUCCESS targets of the same build, and a dead server
# recorded as SUCCESS would hand the retried trainer a dead URL. A
# normal teardown is NOT decided here: launch_skypilot_teardown records
# the cluster as intentionally torn down before downing it, and the
# monitor then ends this target SUCCESS whatever the job's status.
#
# MAX_LIFETIME > 0 arms a watchdog so a stranded server (consumer
# crashed => teardown never eligible) releases its node instead of
# holding it indefinitely. The watchdog is killed on the normal path,
# so it costs a sleeping subshell and nothing else.
MAX_LIFETIME=0
REAPED_FLAG="$(mktemp -u)"
WATCHDOG_PID=""
# A signal to this script cannot be told apart from a teardown's, so the
# trap keeps the status a signal-killed shell reports (128 + signo), says
# why, and takes the server and watchdog down with it.
on_signal() {
  echo "student-rollout-generator: FATAL: received $1 while serving; stopping the vLLM server. Unless the teardown target sent it, this target fails." >&2
  [ -z "$WATCHDOG_PID" ] || kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  exit "$2"
}
trap 'on_signal SIGTERM 143' TERM
trap 'on_signal SIGINT 130' INT
echo "student-rollout-generator: holding the allocation until the teardown target ends it"
if [ "$MAX_LIFETIME" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "student-rollout-generator: lifetime cap ${MAX_LIFETIME}s armed"
  (
    sleep "$MAX_LIFETIME"
    if kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
      : > "$REAPED_FLAG"
      kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  ) &
  WATCHDOG_PID=$!
fi
RC=0; wait "$SERVER_PID" || RC=$?
[ -z "$WATCHDOG_PID" ] || kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
if [ -f "$REAPED_FLAG" ]; then
  rm -f "$REAPED_FLAG"
  echo "student-rollout-generator: FATAL: lifetime cap of ${MAX_LIFETIME}s reached; releasing the allocation. Nothing tore this server down in time — check whether the consumer target failed." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# vLLM exits 0 on a SIGTERM aimed at it, so even a clean exit is a
# failure here: nothing but the teardown target should end this server.
echo "student-rollout-generator: FATAL: the vLLM server exited (rc=$RC) before the teardown target ended it" >&2
[ "$RC" -ne 0 ] || RC=1
exit "$RC"
